title: Foreplay Pricing 2026: Plans, Seats and Credits | Sprites
summary: Foreplay costs $59, $175 or $459 a month in 2026 — $49, $149 and $389 billed annually. What each plan unlocks, the annual catch, and what no plan does.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **$59/mo Basic** , **$175/mo Workflow** , **$459/mo Agency** — or $49, $149 and $389 billed annually.
- **Seven-day free trial, no credit card** , on every self-serve plan. Extra seats are $20 each.
- The annual switch saves ~15% and **lifts the brand-tracking cap to unlimited** — that second part is the real reason to take it.
- No plan connects to an ad account. Foreplay finds and briefs creative; it never launches it.


Prices read from foreplay.co in September 2026.


## The ladder


Plan Monthly Annual /mo Seats What it adds


**Basic** $59 $49 1 Swipe file, Discovery, Briefs, API, MCP


**Workflow** $175 $149 5 + Spyder tracking, Lens on 1 brand


**Agency** $459 $389 10 + Spyder on 50 brands, Lens on 10


**Enterprise** Quote. Unlimited seats, Slack support, early access.


## The annual switch is a cap lift, not a discount


Annual billing takes about 15% off, which is what the page leads with. The number that actually changes your workflow is the tracking cap: monthly plans limit Spyder to 15 brands on Workflow and 50 on Agency, while **annual plans list it as unlimited** and double monthly credits from 10,000 to 20,000.


So the question is not whether 15% matters. It is whether you follow more brands than the monthly cap allows — and if you are an agency, you almost certainly do.


## Which tier you actually need


- **Solo strategist** → Basic. One seat, saving and briefing, no performance data.
- **In-house team** → Workflow. First tier that reads performance through Lens rather than only inspiration.
- **Agency** → Agency, annual. Ten seats, Lens on ten brands, and the cap lift above.


## What they spend that money telling you


Foreplay's own advertising is the clearest statement of who the product is for. Every creative below is running right now, and the whole library is free to browse:


The 315-day evergreen: “Have you heard of Foreplay?” — the longest-running ad in their library.Video is 65% of their wall, most of it creator-posted rather than brand-made.Carousels cluster at two cards, the swipe used as a reveal.


[See all of Foreplay's ads →](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/foreplay) Free, no login, with run dates and destinations on every creative.


## What no plan does


Foreplay does not connect to an ad account to change anything. It finds, organises and briefs creative. Launching the campaign, setting the budget and reallocating it next week happen somewhere else — usually in Ads Manager, by hand.


That is not a flaw, it is the category line. It is also the line to price against: at $459/mo for the Agency tier, the question is what the brief is worth if nothing downstream changes.
